models.name: Continuum Glenoid–Scapula Model (CGSM)
models.what_it_computes: 3D implicit FEA of a cemented polyethylene glenoid with cortical/cancellous scapula and uniform cement layer; computes rim opening/closure displacement, cement hydrostatic tension, contact patch migration, and cement–bone micromotion under eccentric cyclic loading.

models.name: Pegged Interface Cohesive Model (PICM)
models.what_it_computes: Local implicit FEA of a pegged glenoid subassembly with cohesive zone elements at peg–cement and cement–bone interfaces; computes shear/normal tractions, damage variable, slip/opening, and cycles-to-initiation surrogate for interface fatigue during rocking.

mechanisms.name: Rim toggle–induced tensile debonding
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Superior–inferior eccentric loading can open the cement–bone interface at the rim, initiating cracks that propagate and compromise fixation.

mechanisms.name: Peg–cement shear fatigue during rocking
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Alternating shear around pegs can accumulate damage at the peg–cement interface, reducing stability and promoting loosening.

deviation.detail: All factor scores are reported on a four-point 0–12 CredMark-12 scale (0, 4, 8, 12) with narrative anchors.

expected_decision.outcome_source: This credibility assessment of two implicit finite element models for a cemented anatomic glenoid component under rocking-horse loading indicates that each model is well suited to a distinct failure pathway and, in combination, can inform preclinical judgments about loosening risk.
rationale_keywords: comparative risk assessment within the validated envelopes

datasets: cadaveric rocking tests (n = 7 specimens) with digital image correlation (DIC) rim lift-off tracking
requirements: For CGSM use in evaluating relative risk of rim debonding under variant load configurations, scores at or above 8 for the alignment of outputs and for validation similarity, combined with at least 8 for numerical error control and uncertainty characterization, were required for quantitative comparisons across design variants.
For PICM use in assessing peg–cement shear fatigue initiation under mapped toggling amplitudes, scores at or above 8 for interface output relevance and validation mapping were required.
